reviewer.independenceStatement: I performed a process-isolated source and evidence review from 2026-09-15T01:19:00Z through 2026-09-15T04:49:57Z. The candidate was corrected and repackaged during review; this report targets only final package 6f3ab4c0d12f6a3f705d76869703fbddb50ea1d0c30d7667d0dd9199f755b92a and artifact 5896572753484b3f64903b2b4ccc4f0f471ddab33ef034f5c3b1bb1c3d509669. I directly reviewed the bounded archive reader, release and hosted-source controls, signing workflow and policy evidence, bounded compiler-output and owner registries, exact TLS terminal-cleanup source, its public DuplexTransport boundary, the native TCP cleanup case, the peer-waiting custom-transport regression, and the corrected indexed security narrative. I audited the rebuilt daily-SDK artifact and the bound qualification, fuzz, runtime, supply-chain, full-check, and 600-second preflight records but did not rerun their commands. The previous incomplete archive-review attempt is not treated as approval. findings.title: Release archive metadata expanded before resource bounds
findings.reproduction: Verify a gzip tar containing repeated global PAX records, an over-limit member or aggregate payload, excessive serialized headers, or a GNU sparse encoding before a valid release manifest.
findings.impact: The baseline verifier accepted over-limit archives and allowed PAX or sparse metadata processing before a release payload was trusted; the retained allocation probe reached 20,081,071 traced bytes from 410,624 decoded bytes, allowing an untrusted release artifact to exhaust verifier resources before rejection.
findings.evidence: archive-review-controls.json records all seven exact cases failing on baseline 14a9925 and passing on the bounded reader. The separate allocation records show early cumulative-PAX rejection with at most 515,767 traced bytes in the measured 80-block case. The current reader bounds decompressed bytes, expanded payload, raw headers, metadata records, member size, and global and effective PAX fields, and rejects four GNU sparse encodings before map expansion.
findings.fix: Wrap the decompressed stream in a cumulative byte budget, enforce per-member, aggregate, header, metadata, and PAX field limits before extraction, and reject GNU sparse processing at each tar dispatch point.

findings.title: Hosted signature metadata selected the verification source
findings.reproduction: Give the baseline verify-all path a hosted PASS record whose source_revision differs from the separately approved source while cryptographic verification is stubbed successful for the isolated source-selection test.
findings.impact: The baseline used the hosted report itself to select the source digest, so verification could authenticate a different commit without proving that it was the release owner's independently selected source.
findings.evidence: hosted-source-controls.json records the mismatched-hosted-revision case failing on 14a9925 and passing now. The corrected workflow requires the protected environment, exact approved SHA, exact protected tag, and checkout of that SHA; local verification obtains its expected commit from signing-approval.json and rejects different hosted metadata. The fresh live policy capture is PASS and honestly records that no non-administrator enforcement probe was available.
findings.fix: Select the expected commit only from the separately authored approval record, require hosted source_revision equality, and use the exact approved SHA for tag checks, checkout, and attestation verification.

findings.title: Formal and signature inputs were not durable seal inputs
findings.reproduction: Place the formal candidate JSON, soak JSON and raw logs, release manifest, and three Sigstore bundles only in the working tree, then run the baseline verification and seal a task whose source_paths omit those files.
findings.impact: Verification could pass using transient files that a clean clone could not reproduce; the hosted artifact retention was only 90 days, so the durable evidence could outlive neither the workflow artifact nor the original workspace.
findings.evidence: The six-case hosted-source record shows baseline acceptance and current rejection for omitted formal and signing inputs. Corrected verify-all requires all nine generated inputs in the additive task source inventory, after which repository sealing requires their committed candidate bytes. The verifier fails closed before hosted files exist.
findings.fix: Require the five formal JSON and raw-log inputs and the release manifest plus three Sigstore bundles as exact task source paths before production verification can pass, then seal their committed bytes.

findings.title: Frozen candidate preserved only the soak command
findings.reproduction: Keep final-candidate-soak unchanged while removing required_evidence, another acceptance command, or an existing source path after the frozen candidate or after the approved signing source.
findings.impact: The baseline comparison accepted the weakened task because it compared only one command, allowing a later candidate to seal a reduced, self-defined release contract without the original production-signature or evidence obligations.
findings.evidence: hosted-source-controls.json records baseline acceptance and current rejection of weakened task fields and removed source inputs. frozen_command now compares the complete frozen task blob, and verify-all repeats the complete comparison against the approved source; every non-source_paths field and every existing source path is retained, while only additive generated evidence paths are allowed.
findings.fix: Compare the complete committed task contract at the frozen and approved revisions with the current task, reject every non-source_paths change and every removed source path, and permit only additive paths needed for post-freeze evidence.

findings.title: Fixed-length HTTP/1 requests bypassed maxBodyBytes
findings.reproduction: Send a request whose valid Content-Length exceeds HttpLimits.maxBodyBytes and have the handler consume the request body.
findings.impact: A remote peer could make a server handler process a fixed-length request body larger than its configured parser body bound, while chunked HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 enforce the bound.
findings.evidence: The current runtime record binds the exact source, reproduces the oversized fixed-length failure on baseline 50bc5cc, and records the complete corrected HTTP/1 suite passing; this reviewer audited but did not rerun that command.
findings.fix: Compare fixed Content-Length with maxBodyBytes before opening Http1FixedBodyStream and reject an oversized request.

findings.title: Non-reusable HTTP/1 TLS completion used unbounded graceful close
findings.reproduction: Receive a complete non-reusable HTTPS response and have the peer withhold its TLS close notification while keeping the transport open.
findings.impact: Response completion could block indefinitely after request cancellation ownership had already been detached, allowing a remote peer to hang the consumer.
findings.evidence: The current runtime record binds the exact source, reproduces withheld TLS shutdown on baseline 50bc5cc, and records the corrected disposal path in the complete HTTP/1 suite passing; this reviewer audited but did not rerun that command.
findings.fix: Abort transport disposal for non-reusable automatic response completion instead of waiting for peer-driven graceful TLS shutdown without an owner budget.

findings.title: Rejected unpublished HTTP/2 admission retained an unowned stream
findings.reproduction: Close the pool after a newly created connection admits its first stream but before the connection is published in the pool.
findings.impact: Graceful close waited for an admitted registry stream that no returned lease could finish, hanging the acquire and pool-close race.
findings.evidence: The current runtime record binds the exact source, reproduces the unpublished admission owner leak on baseline 50bc5cc, and records the corrected abort path in the complete HTTP/1 suite passing; this reviewer audited but did not rerun that command.
findings.fix: Abort unpublished HTTP/2 connections on admission rejection or setup failure so abort retires the admitted stream registry owner.

findings.title: TLS close deadline could not interrupt pump admission
findings.reproduction: Start a background TLS read or blocked ciphertext write, then close the connection with cancellation or a finite deadline while the first operation owns pump admission.
findings.impact: Close could wait past its deadline on a mutex held across transport I/O, leaving cleanup dependent on a silent peer.
findings.evidence: The current runtime record covers read deadline, read cancellation, write cancellation, concurrent close and abort disposal, and the immediate-cancellation registration cleanup case, with the complete corrected TLS suite passing; this reviewer audited but did not rerun that command.
findings.fix: Use deadline-aware pump admission, terminate admissions during close or abort, interrupt underlying transport I/O, and release the native engine only after read, write, and close owners become idle with cancellation registration inside guaranteed cleanup.

findings.title: Soak owner fields were literal rather than observed
findings.reproduction: Feed the historical soak log with hard-coded owner fields to the baseline verifier, then exercise a growing weak-owner sequence or retained terminal owner with the corrected verifier.
findings.impact: The baseline could report owner coverage without detecting leaks in waiters, buffers, tasks, responses, transports, or cancellation callback graphs.
findings.evidence: The refreshed owner-control record rejects the historical literal-owner schema and growing or terminal owner failures. The current installed-artifact 600-second preflight completed 5,846 cycles with an 18.493331-millisecond maximum cancellation latency, 13,154 balanced pool acquisitions and releases, and zero terminal owners, but remains explicitly non-formal.
findings.fix: Replace literal fields with pool-hook balances, response closure, Future state and joins, wrapped transport I/O, weak transport and cancellation sentinels, bounded growth checks, and exact terminal cleanup assertions.

regressions.command: M8-007 installed-consumer bounded-owner preflight for 600 seconds with 60-second application samples

findings.title: Compiler output was retained without a memory bound
findings.reproduction: Run the clean installed-consumer build with a compiler process that emits more than 16 KiB on success or failure, including invalid UTF-8 bytes.
findings.impact: The baseline captured the complete merged compiler stream in Python memory and copied it into the success report or failure exception, so a noisy build could inflate the release gate process and its evidence without a fixed bound before the formal soak started.
findings.evidence: build-output-controls.json records three failures on baseline 8a603905 and all three passing now. The success and failure controls emitted 2,097,185 and 2,097,167 bytes respectively; the invalid-UTF-8 control exposed replacement expansion. The corrected path writes the complete byte stream to a temporary file, copies complete decoded diagnostics to parent stderr, and retains at most 16 KiB after UTF-8 encoding in the report or exception.
findings.fix: Direct compiler output to a file-backed log, preserve the full decoded stream through parent stderr, and retain only a byte-bounded tail in returned reports and failures.

findings.title: Soak observation registries grew without admission bounds
findings.reproduction: Create 4,096 released response-owner claims without sampling, then separately retain 1,024 cancellation sentinels or 1,024 closed observed transports and attempt one more admission.
findings.impact: The baseline observation arrays admitted every weak reference and cancellation closure. When sampling was delayed or an actual leak kept referents live, the diagnostic harness itself could grow until resource checks became distorted or the formal soak exhausted memory instead of reporting the ownership failure.
findings.evidence: owner-registry-before.json records 4,096 stale slots and accepts a 1,025th live cancellation and transport observation. owner-registry-after.json records a peak of 1,024 stale slots, retains all 1,024 deliberately live referents without eviction, and rejects the extra cancellation and transport admissions. The reviewed source prunes reclaimed entries at admission, caps both tables at 1,024, waits at most two seconds for cancellation reclamation, refuses a full transport table before connecting, and aborts a transport if a concurrent admission fills the last slot after connection.
findings.fix: Prune weak registries when they reach capacity, impose independent 1,024-entry limits, fail closed without evicting live observations, close responses when claim admission fails, and abort a newly opened transport when its final synchronized admission fails.

findings.title: Expired TLS close budget skipped native transport disposal
findings.reproduction: Hold a real native TcpStream read open without peer assistance, call TLS close with a short deadline, and let pump shutdown consume that deadline before terminal transport cleanup begins.
findings.impact: The exact c0f13f5 connection source delegated close with the already-expired context; native transport admission rejected it before disposal, leaving the TCP stream, blocked read, and TLS engine owned after the close returned a timeout.
findings.evidence: runtime-review-controls.json binds the exact c0f13f5 source snapshot and records closeDeadlineReleasesAnExistingNativeTcpReadWithoutPeerAssistance failing there and passing on the corrected source. The corrected case observes TimedOut, a stopped native read, a closed client stream, and one engine release without peer completion. Its controlled TLS engine isolates lifecycle scheduling and is not presented as cryptographic handshake proof.
findings.fix: When the caller context is already cancelled or expired at terminal cleanup, immediately abort the underlying transport with the matching reason rather than attempting graceful close admission through the stopped context; retain guaranteed engine release after all active owners finish.

findings.title: TLS terminal cleanup reset the caller's close budget
findings.reproduction: Use a caller-supplied DuplexTransport whose graceful close waits for peer completion only while its received context has budget, then let TLS pump shutdown exhaust the caller's deadline before terminal cleanup.
findings.impact: The rejected intermediate correction created a context without the caller's deadline or cancellation for terminal transport close. A peer that withheld completion could therefore hang TlsConnection.close indefinitely after the caller's finite budget expired.
findings.evidence: docs/evidence/M8-007/commands/20260915-custom-transport-repro/intermediate-rejected-connection.cj.txt preserves the rejected reset-context source. runtime-review-controls.json binds peerWaitingGracefulCloseStaysBoundedByTheCallerBudget and peerWaitingGracefulCloseCompletesWithinItsBudget to the current source and records the complete TLS suite passing. Source review confirms that live cleanup receives the original context, stopped cleanup aborts immediately, and a context-driven NetworkException is followed by terminal abort with cancellation or deadline priority.
findings.fix: Delegate graceful terminal close only with the original live OperationContext; if it is cancelled, expired, or becomes stopped during delegated close, use immediate abort with the matching reason and preserve the caller's cancellation or timeout result.

findings.title: Indexed TLS cleanup narrative described the rejected design
findings.reproduction: Compare the refreshed security narrative with TlsConnection.close and runtime-review-controls.json after adding the peer-waiting transport case.
findings.impact: The indexed scope said cleanup after budget expiry needed a context that could still admit graceful close, and the README explicitly described a fresh context while claiming only eight original-baseline failures. That endorsed the rejected unbounded peer-wait design, omitted the sixth TLS regression, and contradicted the source reviewers were being asked to approve.
findings.evidence: The final indexed security-scope digest 82a37a555f66d9f816485638bf684867532ca3f5d0695987e48e48420e1c53c7 now names the peer-waiting budget loss and states the original-context-while-live plus immediate-abort-when-stopped rule. README now reports three HTTP/1, six TLS, and one separate native targeted failure and describes the same correction.
findings.fix: Replace the intermediate fresh-context narrative with the exact current lifecycle rule and include the peer-waiting regression in the baseline count and scope.

findings.title: Preflight narrative attributed stale metrics to the current artifact
findings.reproduction: Compare the preflight cycle and maximum-cancellation-latency values in the refreshed narrative with bounded-owner-preflight-600s.json for artifact 5896572753484b3f.
findings.impact: The narrative attributed a previous candidate's 5,870 cycles and 6.008281-millisecond latency to the current artifact even though its bound preflight records 5,846 cycles and 18.493331 milliseconds, breaking the evidence trace between the reviewed package and its retained non-formal run.
findings.evidence: The final security scope and README now state 5,846 cycles, 18.493331 milliseconds, zero terminal owners, and the current artifact identity. The bound preflight digest d2b7cbb4b270e5d66d12785364423a492fc54268544648f1b670e01a81b722fb records the same values and 13,154 balanced pool acquisitions and releases.
findings.fix: Replace the stale summary values with the current artifact's bound preflight measurements and identify the artifact in both narratives.
